## [ASER Distills LLM-Extracted Sensory Attributes for Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02709) ⭐️ 6.0/10

Researchers present ASER (Attribute-based Sensory-Enhanced Representation), an offline pipeline that fine-tunes a large language model to extract evidence-grounded sensory attribute-value records (e.g., color: matte black, scent: vanilla) from review text and distills them into a compact student encoder that produces a frozen five-facet sensory bank per item catalog. Across five Amazon domains and four backbones, this integration improves HR@10 and NDCG@10 in all 20 domain-backbone pairs, with average relative gains of 6.1% and 6.4%. Sequential recommenders typically rely on item identifiers and behavioral signals, leaving the experiential properties users describe in reviews largely outside item representations; ASER shows these sensory signals can be injected in a controlled, auditable way without retraining the backbone. The approach could benefit e-commerce and other domains where subjective product experience drives user preference, and it offers a reusable recipe for turning unstructured review text into structured recommendation features. At recommendation time the pretrained backbone stays frozen: a lightweight relational metric between user history and each candidate is learned over the sensory bank, and its correction is applied within a validation-selected magnitude bound. A matched non-sensory control channel separates the sources of gain — structured, evidence-grounded extraction drives the hit-rate improvement, while the sensory vocabulary yields a ranking-quality advantage in eight of nine matched comparisons; an audit of the Beauty catalog finds 94.8% of retained records are supported by their cited evidence spans.

## [KD-Brain: Prior-Informed Graph Learning for Brain Subnetwork Interactions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19307) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper introduces KD-Brain, a prior-informed graph learning framework that explicitly encodes prior knowledge to guide the modeling of subnetwork interactions in heterogeneous brain networks. It features a Semantic-Conditioned Interaction mechanism that injects semantic priors into attention queries, and a Pathology-Consistent Constraint that aligns learned interaction distributions with clinical priors, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple mental disorder diagnosis tasks. This work addresses a key limitation of Transformer-based methods for brain network analysis—their reliance on large training samples—by incorporating domain knowledge, which could lead to more accurate and interpretable diagnoses of mental disorders. KD-Brain explicitly navigates subnetwork interactions based on their functional identities via semantic-conditioned attention, and regularizes optimization with a pathology-consistent constraint. The code is available at an anonymous repository, and the method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of disorder diagnosis tasks while yielding interpretable biomarkers.

## [CoMemNet: Continual Memory Network with Drift-Aware Sampling for Traffic Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05738) ⭐️ 6.0/10

Researchers propose CoMemNet, a continual memory network for traffic prediction over evolving sensor networks, combining an Online branch, an EMA Target branch, a Wasserstein-based Drift Sampler, and a lightweight Node-Adaptive Temporal Memory Replay Buffer (TMRB-N). Experiments on three multi-period PeMS datasets with three-seed evaluation show stable accuracy and efficient adaptation, with growing advantages in accuracy and cumulative training time over current-period retraining baselines as the network expands. Real-world traffic sensor networks constantly add and remove sensors and see distribution shifts, yet most forecasting models assume a fixed node set and retrain on all historical data, which is costly and prone to catastrophic forgetting. CoMemNet offers a scalable continual learning recipe that preserves historical knowledge while adapting to the current period, which could benefit large-scale intelligent transportation systems and other evolving sensor deployments. The prediction backbone does not consume an adjacency matrix; sensor adjacency is used only to construct data and optionally expand the selected update set to a limited neighborhood. The Drift Sampler compares node-wise Online-Target feature distributions via Wasserstein distance to select a bounded set of drift-sensitive nodes, and TMRB-N retains compact temporal states without repeatedly traversing all historical training data.

## [GPart: Isometric Fine-Tuning via Global Parameter Partitioning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14841) ⭐️ 6.0/10

Researchers propose GPart (Global Partition fine-tuning), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that maps a d-dimensional trainable vector directly into the full weight space through a sparse, isometric partition matrix. Unlike LoRA, whose bilinear parameterization breaks end-to-end isometry, GPart achieves exact end-to-end isometry with a single hyperparameter (d) and a minimal checkpoint consisting of the trainable vector plus a random seed. GPart offers a mathematically tractable and memory-efficient alternative to LoRA-based PEFT, matching or improving performance at ultra-low parameter budgets across natural language understanding, computer vision, and mathematical reasoning benchmarks. Its direct linear parameterization could simplify model selection and enable compact adapter composition, benefiting researchers and practitioners working on efficient fine-tuning of large models. GPart removes the additional low-rank reconstruction used by LoRA-based methods and relies on a fixed global parameter-sharing prior, with the trainable vector and a random seed forming the entire checkpoint. The method builds on the premise that effective fine-tuning can occur within random low-dimensional subspaces of the full weight space without requiring low-rank matrix factorization.

**Background**: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) adapts large pre-trained models to new tasks by updating only a small fraction of parameters, reducing memory and compute costs. LoRA is a dominant PEFT technique that freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable low-rank decomposition matrices into Transformer layers, but its bilinear parameterization means the mapping from trainable parameters to weight updates is not distance-preserving (non-isometric). Isometric mappings preserve distances between points, and prior work such as Uni-LoRA projects a low-dimensional vector into LoRA's parameter space but still suffers from the subsequent non-isometric bilinear map.

## [TEGER: Test-Time Residual Covariance for Traffic Forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18068) ⭐️ 6.0/10

TEGER introduces a residual covariance model that refreshes a forecaster's joint predictive uncertainty at test time using closed-form Gaussian conditioning and an exponential moving-average volatility term, without retraining the backbone. On four traffic datasets it improves 60-minute CRPS_sum over a temporal-only baseline, and applied post hoc to the frozen time-series foundation model Chronos it reduces CRPS_sum from 0.1798 to 0.1736. Traffic conditions drift over a deployment's lifetime, so uncertainty estimates fixed at training time become miscalibrated, and this work shows that a lightweight test-time correction can keep them current at negligible added cost. Because the mechanism never touches the backbone's weights, it can be attached to frozen time-series foundation models, turning a static point forecast into one with continually refreshed, correlated uncertainty. A fixed sensor graph supplies a low-dimensional spatial precision factor encoding which sensors' errors move together, and at inference Gaussian conditioning corrects the next forecast's mean and covariance from only the most recently observed residuals. An exponential moving-average volatility term rescales marginal uncertainty to track local drift while preserving the learned correlation structure, and no gradient passes through the frozen backbone.

## [Morpheus: A Morphology-Aware Neural Tokenizer and Word Embedder for Turkish](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18717) ⭐️ 6.0/10

Researchers released Morpheus, a neural morpheme-boundary model for Turkish that acts simultaneously as a lossless tokenizer and a word embedder, using a differentiable Poisson-binomial dynamic program to convert per-character boundary probabilities into soft morpheme memberships during training and exact segments at inference. Among reversible tokenizers it achieves the lowest bits-per-character (1.425), roughly doubles gold morphological alignment versus subword tokenizers (MorphScore macro-F1 0.61 vs. ~0.32), and uses about 19% less GPU memory than 64K-vocabulary subword tokenizers. Morpheus offers a reversible, morphology-aware alternative that could improve NLP for morphologically rich languages and provides a reusable recipe for combining tokenization with embedding learning. The model guarantees decode(encode(w)) = w by construction with no string normalization, and the same forward pass that tokenizes also emits a structured word embedding. As an embedder, frozen Morpheus vectors lead on lexical retrieval (root-family MAP 0.85) and same-root verification (ROC-AUC 1.00), surpassing BGE-M3 and BERTurk, but heavier contextual encoders remain ahead on context- and inflection-dependent tasks such as NER and case/number probing, a trade-off attributed to Morpheus's root-centric geometry.

An arXiv paper (2606.27090v2) introduces two mathematical tools—the Mass Index and regularised extended KL (RE-KL)—to study distributional local-mass behaviours that global objectives like KL divergence and ELBO fail to capture. It proves absolute, relative, and directional inequalities for comparing local small-ball masses under the two KL directions, with experiments showing the directional comparison remains visible in variational posteriors of Bayesian neural networks up to ResNet-50 on ImageNet. This work offers a local theoretical account that complements global divergence measures widely used in Bayesian inference and variational methods, potentially improving how researchers diagnose and compare posterior approximations. It could influence theoretical statistics and the design of variational inference algorithms, especially for Bayesian neural networks where local mass behaviour matters. The Mass Index records polynomial and logarithmic decay scales of local mass, and RE-KL is a set-localised divergence that can be formulated even in the presence of singular components. The paper shows that power-log likelihood factors shift local mass explicitly, while parameter-dependent supports or their smooth softenings may change the local scale through the amount of mass remaining near the parameter value; code is available on GitHub.

## [MASCIT: Mask-Aware State Space Classifier for Irregular Time Series](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34409) ⭐️ 6.0/10

A new arXiv paper (2609.34409v2) introduces MASCIT, a mask-aware state space classifier that feeds observation masks into the encoder and excludes invalid steps from gated temporal aggregation. Across 34 irregular time series datasets, MASCIT achieved the strongest aggregate point estimate and was the only evaluated neural model with three-seed results on every dataset. Naturally irregular time series are common in healthcare, climate, and sensor networks, where standard dense models often discard temporal structure. By showing that selective state space models can serve as effective, executable backbones for such data, MASCIT offers a practical direction for improving classification robustness in real-world irregular sampling settings. MASCIT retained the lowest point rank across six overlapping irregularity indicators, and factorial ablations favored partial over full selectivity. The paper reports three-seed results on all 34 datasets, though it remains a niche arXiv preprint without community discussion or a released implementation noted in the abstract.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Oct 5, 04:00

**Background**: Irregular time series combine asynchronous observations, missing values, unequal lengths, and nonuniform sampling, which breaks the fixed-interval assumptions of many classical models. State space models describe a system's hidden state evolving over time and are well suited to sequential data, while gated temporal aggregation selectively combines information across time steps. Observation masks explicitly mark which time steps contain valid data, allowing a model to ignore missing or invalid entries rather than treating them as real values.

## [ARGOS Uses Reinforcement Learning for Multidimensional Elasticity in Computing Continuum](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37085) ⭐️ 6.0/10

ARGOS (Adaptive Reinforcement Learning-Driven Governance for Orchestrated Services) is an end-to-end controller that formulates multidimensional elasticity as a per-request Markov decision process over analytics quality and cluster pressure, supported by capacity-aware admission. Evaluated on a heterogeneous cluster under controlled and time-varying multi-tenant workloads, its deep reinforcement learning policies consistently outperform non-learning baselines and approach the independently tuned best-fixed reference, with no CPU or memory violations but remaining coverage violations. This work addresses a real gap in computing continuum orchestration: existing orchestrators mainly adapt resources, placements, or replicas while analytics requirements such as coverage, sample, and freshness remain fixed. By showing that deep reinforcement learning can adapt analytics quality itself when resource scaling alone is insufficient, ARGOS points toward more autonomous service governance across edge-cloud heterogeneous environments. ARGOS treats elasticity as a per-request Markov decision process and adds capacity-aware admission control, and it is evaluated both under controlled workloads and in a separate live evaluation with realistic and saturated arrivals. The live evaluation reports improvements over the static midpoint, but coverage violations remain, indicating that quality guarantees are not yet fully satisfied.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Oct 5, 04:00

**Background**: The computing continuum refers to a diverse array of distributed devices, from IoT and edge nodes to cloud data centers, working together to meet application demands. A Markov decision process (MDP) is a mathematical framework for sequential decision making under uncertainty, characterized by states, actions, and rewards, and it underlies reinforcement learning. Multidimensional elasticity extends the traditional notion of scaling resources by also adapting analytics requirements such as coverage, sample, and freshness.

## [Audit Reveals Fragility in Long-Term Memory Retrieval Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38021) ⭐️ 6.0/10

A new arXiv paper audits the evaluation of a long-term-memory retrieval chain on the 500-question LongMemEval-S benchmark, showing that re-judging the same answers changes labels, reader lanes vary from 93 to 479, and a different-family reader scores 474 versus the 479 headline. The audit also finds that a negative control rejects a verifier that repairs three wrong drafts but breaks eleven correct ones, and that no untouched holdout was ever evaluated. This work matters because it shows that headline scores on long-term memory benchmarks can be unstable and non-reproducible, which undermines leaderboard comparisons and could mislead practitioners choosing memory systems. It calls for more robust evaluation protocols, including pinned reader snapshots, repeated judging, and untouched holdouts. The strongest historical reader lane scores 479 and 475 under an adapted GPT-4o rubric, and re-judging the same pass-1 answers changes three labels to yield 478; fixed-answer knowledge-update re-scoring gives 70/72 under the upstream template and 69/72 under a modified template. The full package scores 474 versus 454 for baseline sessions, a +4.0 percentage point difference, but 18 of 23 gains occur where baseline packets lacked listed evidence, so this post-hoc split does not identify a component effect.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Oct 5, 04:00

**Background**: LongMemEval is a benchmark designed to test chat assistants' long-term memory across multi-session dialogues, with the LongMemEval-S variant containing 500 questions and histories averaging around 115,000 tokens. Evaluation often uses an LLM-as-judge with a rubric, such as an adapted GPT-4o rubric, to score answers. This audit examines whether such scores are stable across repeated judging, different reader models, and template changes, and whether reported gains reflect real memory advantages.

## [Google to cut free Gemini down to Flash-Lite starting October 9](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/17004136?hl=en) ⭐️ 6.0/10

Starting October 9, Google will remove the Flash and Pro models from free Gemini accounts in the Gemini app, leaving only Flash-Lite available to free users. Paid tiers keep broader access: AI Plus retains Flash-Lite and Flash, while AI Pro and Ultra keep all three models. This change narrows what free users can do with Gemini, pushing more capable reasoning and multimodal models behind paid subscriptions and reinforcing the industry trend of monetizing advanced AI capabilities. It directly affects the large base of free Gemini users and may push some toward Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra plans, or toward competing free-tier chatbots. Flash-Lite is positioned as the fastest and most budget-friendly model in Google's Gemini family, optimized for simple, high-frequency tasks rather than complex reasoning. The rollout begins October 9 and is described as a gradual removal, so exact timing may vary by account and region.
